analysis:
Vaishnaw said in March 2024 that India would be among the top five semiconductor manufacturing countries within five years, as construction began on the Dholera fab and on packaging and testing units in Gujarat and Assam.

Later government and industry reports state that the Dholera front-end fabrication plant is expected to be operational around 2028, that several assembly, testing and packaging units have started commercial production, and that in 2026 five of twelve approved units were producing commercially.

Large-scale chip fabrication is currently concentrated in Taiwan, South Korea, China, the United States and Japan. India is not presently among the largest chip manufacturing economies, and the target window runs to about 2029-2030, so the claim is in progress.

The promise says 'within the next five years' (about 2029) while the ET headline frames it as 'by 2030'; deadline set to 2030-03-31. There is some ambiguity between front-end fab production and back-end assembly/test production in Indian reporting.
